query: What does Couloir claim to jointly optimize under shared K and C?
snippet:
TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving.
TOPAS schedules a joint GPU state: resident agent KV prefixes plus admitted requests, rather than selecting requests individually.
It enforces shared-prefix cost once per agent plus per-request dynamic KV/output/decode reservations against available capacity.
Its score balances workflow-DAG progress, prefix movement, preemption, one-hop downstream reuse, and task aging; GreedyPack allocates requests for each candidate prefix set.
Objective: minimize average task-level JCT under online arrivals.
TOPAS is the closest systems peer to Couloir's joint compute+cache framing, but is an engine-level joint state scheduler with real KV capacity constraints rather than a discrete-event sim with conceptual C.
title: TOPAS (arXiv:2608.25523)

query: What does Couloir claim to jointly optimize under shared K and C?
snippet:
KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows.
KVFlow introduces an Agent Step Graph and steps-to-execution (STE) for workflow-aware prefix-cache eviction.
AND dependencies use max(predecessor STE)+1; conditional/OR branches use min(predecessor STE)+1.
Smaller STE means an agent is closer to reuse, so fixed-prefix KV nodes get higher retention priority; shared radix nodes use the least-evictable child priority.
KVFlow also proactively prefetches likely-next agents' CPU-backed KV during current GPU execution, and uses status-aware scheduling that can skip requests whose nodes are still loading.
Focus: cache residency / prefetch for multi-agent workflows. Ready-queue compute priority is largely external to the STE cache policy.
title: KVFlow (arXiv:2507.07400)

snippet:
SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs (Zheng et al.).
RadixAttention automatically reuses KV caches by storing prompt and generated-token sequences in a radix tree.

query: How does Continuum TTL decide how long to pin KV after tool calls?
snippet:
Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live.
Continuum retains an agent request's KV cache after a tool call by assigning a TTL based on observed tool-duration distributions and reload/queueing costs.
The scheduler pins blocks until TTL expiry, prioritizes returning requests within TTL, and frees them when the program ends or memory pressure requires eviction.
Cost/benefit model: Cost(tau,r) from memory opportunity cost; Benefit from avoided cache-miss prefill/reload and out-of-order queueing delay.
Continuum targets multi-turn tool-using agents and inter-request intervals, not DAG-wide joint dispatch+prefetch under multi-workflow batch arrivals.
title: Continuum (arXiv:2511.02230)
